scene.label: Act 5, Scene 5
scene.title: SCENE V. Dunsinane. Within the castle.

content.text: Enter with drum and colours, Macbeth, Seyton and Soldiers.

lines.text: Hang out our banners on the outward walls;
lines.plainText: Hang out our banners on the outward walls

lines.text: The cry is still, "They come!" Our castle's strength
lines.plainText: The cry is still They come Our castle's strength

lines.text: Will laugh a siege to scorn: here let them lie
lines.plainText: Will laugh a siege to scorn here let them lie

lines.text: Till famine and the ague eat them up.
lines.plainText: Till famine and the ague eat them up

lines.text: Were they not forc'd with those that should be ours,
lines.plainText: Were they not forc'd with those that should be ours

lines.text: We might have met them dareful, beard to beard,
lines.plainText: We might have met them dareful beard to beard

lines.text: And beat them backward home.
lines.plainText: And beat them backward home

lines.text: It is the cry of women, my good lord.
lines.plainText: It is the cry of women my good lord

lines.text: I have almost forgot the taste of fears.
lines.plainText: I have almost forgot the taste of fears

lines.text: The time has been, my senses would have cool'd
lines.plainText: The time has been my senses would have cool'd

lines.text: To hear a night-shriek; and my fell of hair
lines.plainText: To hear a nightshriek and my fell of hair

lines.text: Would at a dismal treatise rouse and stir
lines.plainText: Would at a dismal treatise rouse and stir

lines.text: As life were in't. I have supp'd full with horrors;
lines.plainText: As life were in't I have supp'd full with horrors

lines.text: Direness, familiar to my slaughterous thoughts,
lines.plainText: Direness familiar to my slaughterous thoughts

lines.text: Cannot once start me.
lines.plainText: Cannot once start me

lines.text: The Queen, my lord, is dead.
lines.plainText: The Queen my lord is dead

lines.text: She should have died hereafter.
lines.plainText: She should have died hereafter

lines.text: There would have been a time for such a word.
lines.plainText: There would have been a time for such a word

lines.text: Tomorrow, and tomorrow, and tomorrow,
lines.plainText: Tomorrow and tomorrow and tomorrow

lines.text: Creeps in this petty pace from day to day,
lines.plainText: Creeps in this petty pace from day to day

lines.text: To the last syllable of recorded time;
lines.plainText: To the last syllable of recorded time

lines.text: And all our yesterdays have lighted fools
lines.plainText: And all our yesterdays have lighted fools

lines.text: The way to dusty death. Out, out, brief candle!
lines.plainText: The way to dusty death Out out brief candle

lines.text: Life's but a walking shadow; a poor player,
lines.plainText: Life's but a walking shadow a poor player

lines.text: That struts and frets his hour upon the stage,
lines.plainText: That struts and frets his hour upon the stage

lines.text: And then is heard no more: it is a tale
lines.plainText: And then is heard no more it is a tale

lines.text: Told by an idiot, full of sound and fury,
lines.plainText: Told by an idiot full of sound and fury

lines.text: Signifying nothing.
lines.plainText: Signifying nothing

lines.text: Gracious my lord,
lines.plainText: Gracious my lord

lines.text: I should report that which I say I saw,
lines.plainText: I should report that which I say I saw

lines.text: But know not how to do't.
lines.plainText: But know not how to do't

lines.text: Well, say, sir.
lines.plainText: Well say sir

lines.text: As I did stand my watch upon the hill,
lines.plainText: As I did stand my watch upon the hill

lines.text: I look'd toward Birnam, and anon, methought,
lines.plainText: I look'd toward Birnam and anon methought

lines.text: The wood began to move.
lines.plainText: The wood began to move

lines.text: Liar, and slave!
lines.plainText: Liar and slave

lines.text: Let me endure your wrath, if't be not so.
lines.plainText: Let me endure your wrath if't be not so

lines.text: Within this three mile may you see it coming;
lines.plainText: Within this three mile may you see it coming

lines.text: I say, a moving grove.
lines.plainText: I say a moving grove

lines.text: If thou speak'st false,
lines.plainText: If thou speak'st false

lines.text: Upon the next tree shalt thou hang alive,
lines.plainText: Upon the next tree shalt thou hang alive

lines.text: Till famine cling thee: if thy speech be sooth,
lines.plainText: Till famine cling thee if thy speech be sooth

lines.text: I care not if thou dost for me as much.—
lines.plainText: I care not if thou dost for me as much

lines.text: I pull in resolution; and begin
lines.plainText: I pull in resolution and begin

lines.text: To doubt th' equivocation of the fiend,
lines.plainText: To doubt th' equivocation of the fiend

lines.text: That lies like truth. "Fear not, till Birnam wood
lines.plainText: That lies like truth Fear not till Birnam wood

lines.text: Do come to Dunsinane;" and now a wood
lines.plainText: Do come to Dunsinane and now a wood

lines.text: Comes toward Dunsinane.—Arm, arm, and out!—
lines.plainText: Comes toward DunsinaneArm arm and out

lines.text: If this which he avouches does appear,
lines.plainText: If this which he avouches does appear

lines.text: There is nor flying hence nor tarrying here.
lines.plainText: There is nor flying hence nor tarrying here

lines.text: I 'gin to be aweary of the sun,
lines.plainText: I 'gin to be aweary of the sun

lines.text: And wish th' estate o' th' world were now undone.—
lines.plainText: And wish th' estate o' th' world were now undone

lines.text: Ring the alarum bell!—Blow, wind! come, wrack!
lines.plainText: Ring the alarum bellBlow wind come wrack

lines.text: At least we'll die with harness on our back.
lines.plainText: At least we'll die with harness on our back
